info.title: Alpha Cargo TMS API
info.description:
The Alpha Cargo TMS API for integrators.

Every server-side request is signed with your organization's API key; see
[Authentication](https://docs.alphacargo.io/tms/authentication).

## Errors

A failed request answers with a non-2xx status and `{ "error": "<message>" }`.
The message is localized per `Accept-Language` (`en`, `th`, `zh`).

Organizations set up for the legacy format, and requests sending
`X-Legacy-Response: true`, get every response in the legacy
envelope instead: HTTP 200 with `{ code, message, data, extra, success }`.
Its `code` is one of:

| code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1000` | Invalid parameters |
| `1001` | Unknown merchant / missing organization context |
| `1002` | Invalid signature |
| `1003` | Waybill already exists |
| `1004` | Origin could not be matched |
| `1005` | Destination could not be matched |
| `1006` | Waybill not found |
| `1007` | No carrier assigned |
| `1008` | Package already exists |
| `-1` | System error |

signature.name: api_key
signature.description: Organization API key + HMAC-SHA256 signature. `api_key`, `nonceStr` and `sign` travel beside the business fields: in the JSON body for POST/PATCH/DELETE, in the query string for GET. See https://docs.alphacargo.io/tms/authentication.

bearer.description: Session token of a user signed in to the TMS web app.

owner_id.description: User ID of the organization owner.

settings.description: Organization preferences; the shape is internal.

Organization.description: The organization the request authenticated as. Unlisted fields are internal and may change without notice.

error.description: Human-readable message, localized per Accept-Language (en, th, zh).

id.description: Send this as `X-Sender-Account-Id` on sender-scoped routes.

sender_code.description: System-assigned account code, unique per organization.

slug.description: Your own alternate account code (e.g. from a previous system).

SenderAccount.description: A customer (shipper) account of your organization.

offset.description: The `offset` you sent (or the default), as sent.

page.description: The page actually returned: floor(offset / limit) + 1.

type.description: branch, warehouse, office, hub, division or department.

organization.description: The owning organization, same shape as GET /api/organizations.

OrganizationUnit.description: A branch, warehouse, hub or other location of your organization, with its address.

lat.description: For lat+lng and url input, the caller's own point echoed back.

confidence.description: 0–1. Free text only returns Google matches at ≥ 0.68; `postal_centroid` is always 0.55 and `province_centroid` 0.32. lat+lng and url results are returned at whatever Google's precision gives (0.2–0.95). Treat < 0.68 as unreliable.

source.description: Which step matched. `postal_centroid` / `province_centroid` are area centers, not the address itself; lat+lng and url input always give `google_geocoding`.

ResolvedAddress.description: Component names come in the language picked by `country` (Thai by default), except `province` on a `province_centroid` result, which is the English name.

address.description: Free-text address. Used when neither lat+lng nor url is given; must be non-blank.

url.description: Google Maps link (full or maps.app.goo.gl / goo.gl short link). Other hosts are rejected with 400. The coordinates are read from the link (short-link redirects are followed only while they stay on Google Maps hosts) and reverse-geocoded. Used when lat+lng is absent; must be non-blank.

lat.description: Latitude to reverse-geocode. Must be a JSON number and sent together with lng; takes precedence over url and address.

lng.description: Longitude to reverse-geocode. Must be a JSON number and sent together with lat.

country.description: ISO-2 country hint (e.g. TH, VN, CN). Biases the geocoder's region, picks the response language (TH→Thai, VN→Vietnamese, CN→Chinese, others English; omitted → Thai) and scopes the postal/province fallbacks. Without it the cascade biases toward Thailand.

logResolution.description: Record the resolution in the internal resolution log. Only `false` disables it; default true.

name.description: Subdistrict (tambon) name in the local language.

code.description: The subdistrict's postal code (not an administrative code).

name.description: District (amphoe) name in the local language.
Province name in the local language.

RegionHierarchy.description: Three levels keyed `provinces` → `cities` → `districts`, which hold province → district → subdistrict. Entries are not sorted.

route_id.description: Your organization's route for the waybill.
Your organization's route for the waybill; null when you have none. Each organization on the delegation chain has its own.

Waybill.description: A waybill with its recipient, sender and packages. The response carries more fields than listed here; unlisted fields are internal and may change without notice.

state.description: The event's cross-border milestone (a `SecondaryEventType`, e.g. `customs_finished`) when it has one, otherwise its status.

stateText.description: The milestone's or status's English title, e.g. `Export Customs Cleared`.

code.description: 0 on success; see the error code table.

LegacyEnvelope.description: Legacy response envelope. Always HTTP 200; check `success` and `code`. Used by organizations configured for the legacy format, by requests sending `X-Legacy-Response: true`, and always by POST /api/waybills/{waybillNo}/packages.

volume_util.description: 0–1 share of the vehicle's inside volume used.

payload_kg.description: kg; null when the vehicle type has no payload set.

weight_util.description: 0–1 share of payload; null without a payload.

reason.description: `missing_dimensions`: left out of the plan. `suspect_units`: dimensions look like metres rather than cm; left out. `missing_weight`: planned with an assumed weight.

LoadPlanCargoProblem.description: A package that could not be planned, or was planned with an assumed value.

status.description: `fits`: every unit placed. `partial`: some placed. `none`: nothing placed. `unusable`: the engine could not evaluate the cargo. `no_cargo`: no package has usable dimensions.

basic.description: True when a simpler fallback packer answered because the main engine was unavailable.

details.description: With `validation_failed`: messages per field name. An unknown field is named with the message `Unknown field`.

problems.description: Present with `no_cargo`: why each package was left out.

waybill_ids.description: Waybill IDs (not numbers), at most 500. Unknown IDs are ignored.

vehicle_type_id.description: Vehicle type to check against. Defaults to the delivery's vehicle type when `delivery_id` is given.

delivery_id.description: Existing delivery the waybills would join; its current cargo is included in the check.

LoadPlanFitCheckRequest.description: `vehicle_type_id` or `delivery_id` is required. Unknown fields are rejected; the signature fields (`api_key`, `nonceStr`, `sign`) are allowed beside them.

index.description: Vehicle index in the plan; the display order.

weightUtil.description: 0–1 share of payload; null when the vehicle type has no payload.

splitWaybillIds.description: Waybills the engine spread over more than one vehicle; left out of every group.

fingerprint.description: Opaque hash of the cargo and vehicles the proposal was computed from.

id.description: Delivery ID; use it with the plan endpoint.

planned.description: False when the delivery was created but its load plan could not be computed; compute it later.

waybill_ids.description: Waybill IDs, at most 500. Unknown IDs are ignored.

vehicle_type_ids.description: Vehicle types the split may use.

objective.description: `fewest_vehicles`: fewest vehicles in total. `smallest_vehicles`: prefer filling small vehicles.

max_vehicles.description: Most vehicles in total; the proposal may use fewer. At most 20.

keep_recipient_together.description: Keep each recipient's cargo in one vehicle. Otherwise each waybill is kept in one vehicle.

LoadPlanSplitProposeRequest.description: Propose a split. Nothing is created.

service_id.description: FTL service every created delivery runs under.

groups.description: One delivery per group, at most 20. A waybill may appear in only one group.

LoadPlanSplitAcceptRequest.description: Create one delivery per group, then compute each one's load plan. The groups are re-checked, not trusted. If any delivery fails to create, those already created by this request are removed.

stop_seq.description: 1 = first stop; null when the waybill has no stop order.

manifest.description: The packages planned; `index` links them to placements.

containers.description: Per-vehicle placements as returned by the engine. The shape is not stable.

LoadPlan.description: A saved load plan version. Unlisted fields are internal and may change without notice.

freshness.description: `missing`: no plan. `fresh`: matches the delivery's cargo and vehicle. `stale`: recompute it.

staleReason.description: Why the plan is stale, e.g. `waybill_added`, `waybill_removed`, `stop_order_changed`, `packages_changed`, `vehicle_type_changed`, `no_vehicle_type`, `inputs_changed`.

problems.description: Packages that cannot be planned with the delivery's current cargo.

DeliveryEventType.description: The waybill statuses other than `draft`, which no event can record.

SecondaryEventType.description: A cross-border milestone. Each is recorded as one `event_type`, which sets the package status: `transport_collecting` → `picked_up`, `customs_finished` → `in_transit_hub_outbound`, `transport_originalport` → `in_transit_sorted`, `transport_departed` → `in_transit_hub_outbound`, `transport_arrived` → `in_transit_hub_inbound`, `transport_finished` → `in_transit_sorted`, `transport_handover` → `delivered`.

DeliveryEvent.description: A recorded delivery event. Unlisted fields are internal and may change without notice.

messages.description: First the conflict, then one line per existing later event (ID, type, time).

waybill_id.description: Waybill ID (not the waybill number). Records the event on every package of the waybill. Ignored when `package_id` is given.

package_id.description: Package ID (not the package number). Records the event on that package only; takes precedence over `waybill_id`.

event_time.description: When it happened (ISO 8601). Defaults to now. An unparseable value fails with 400.

coordinates.description: Point as `"x,y"` or `"(x,y)"`; send latitude first, e.g. `"13.7563,100.5018"`.

photos.description: Proof-of-delivery photos as data URLs (`data:image/<type>;base64,...`). Stored with the created event.

ignore_conflicts.description: `true`: record the event even when a later event already exists. The package status is then still updated.

DeliveryEventCreateRequest.description: Either `waybill_id` or `package_id` is required, and `event_type` or `secondary_event_type`.

quotation_id.description: The saved quotation; use it to read, pay or cancel the quote.

max_payload_kg.description: Rated payload, rounded to whole kg.

vehicle.description: The vehicle priced. Null for a multi-vehicle composition, and when the winning price is not tied to a vehicle.

vehicles.description: Multi-vehicle composition, offered when no single vehicle fits the cargo. Null for an ordinary quote.

estimated_total.description: Quoted price; for a composition, the sum of the vehicle prices.

expires_at.description: When the quote stops being valid; 30 minutes unless the carrier sets its own expiry.

error.description: Error code. Note that internal errors (500) also report `missing_required_field`.

post.description:
Turns one of three inputs into a structured address and coordinates: `lat`+`lng` (reverse geocode), `url` (Google Maps link), or `address` (free text). When several are sent, the first present in that order wins.

Free text runs a cascade and returns the first step that matches: Google Geocoding (≥ 0.68), Google Places (0.75), Geocoding on the administrative parts only (≥ 0.68), postal-code centroid (0.55), province centroid (0.32). Always check `confidence` and `source` before using the coordinates — a centroid can be far from the real address.

Requires authentication (signature or session) but no plan feature or user permission.
Error messages are fixed English strings, not localized.

400.description: Body is not JSON; `lat`/`lng` out of range; `url` is not a Google Maps link (https google.<tld>/maps, maps.google.<tld>, maps.app.goo.gl or goo.gl/maps); or none of the inputs given (lat+lng as numbers, or a non-blank url or address).

401.description: No valid signature or session. Body is `{ "error": "Unauthorized" }`.

404.description: Not resolved: no coordinates in the link, Google has no result for the point, or every cascade step missed (low-confidence Google matches are discarded, not returned).

500.description: Geocoder misconfigured or Google unreachable. The error is not caught by the route, so the body is not the JSON error shape.

Requires authentication (signature or session) but no plan feature or user permission.
The response is the bare object, not wrapped in `data`.

patch.description: Updates a package after creation, e.g. at warehouse inbound: weight (kg), length, width, height (cm), description (`itemDesc`), `photos` and `load_properties`. Only the fields sent change; send at least one. Works in any waybill status. A weight or dimension change recomputes the waybill's weight and volume, may re-select the service, and re-prices the waybill's charges; the other fields don't affect totals or charges. Always answers in the legacy envelope with HTTP 200: check `success` and `code` (`1000` invalid parameters, waybill or package not found, `-1` system error).

post.summary: Check whether waybills fit one vehicle
post.description: Packs the waybills' packages (plus a delivery's current cargo, with `delivery_id`) into one vehicle of the given type and reports the result. Nothing is saved. Stop order is ignored. Packages need dimensions (cm) to be planned. Requires the `delivery.planning` plan feature; a signed-in user also needs the `deliveries` permission.

200.description: The fit result. `status: no_cargo` is a 200, not an error.

400.description: Body is not JSON (`invalid_json`) or fails validation (`validation_failed`).

401.description: No valid signature or session.

403.description: The plan lacks `delivery.planning`, or the signed-in user lacks the `deliveries` permission.

404.description: `not_found`: `delivery_id` does not exist or is not visible to you.

422.description: `no_vehicle_type`: no vehicle type given, the delivery has none, or it does not exist.

503.description: `load_planning_unavailable`: the load-planning engine is temporarily unavailable. Retry after the `Retry-After` header (30 seconds).

post.summary: Propose or create a multi-vehicle split
post.description: `action: propose` spreads the waybills over the given vehicle types, one group per vehicle, and creates nothing. `action: accept` creates one delivery per group and computes each delivery's load plan. Requires the `delivery.planning` plan feature; a signed-in user also needs the `deliveries` permission.

400.description: Body is not JSON (`invalid_json`) or fails validation (`validation_failed`).

401.description: No valid signature or session.

post.description:
Records a tracking event and moves the package status to `event_type`. Requires the `delivery.tracking` plan feature; a signed-in user also needs the `deliveries` or `scan` permission.

With `waybill_id` the event is recorded on each package of the waybill and the response carries the event of the first package. Every package is checked first: a conflict on any of them fails the request with 409 and records nothing.

An event conflicts when the package already has an event of a later stage, or any event at or after `event_time`.

If photos fail to upload, the event is still created: the response is 201 with `_podUploadError` set.

_podUploadError.description: Present when the event was created but its photos failed to upload.

schema.description: A recorded delivery event. Unlisted fields are internal and may change without notice.

403.description: The plan lacks `delivery.tracking`, or the signed-in user lacks the `deliveries` and `scan` permissions.

404.description: The waybill or package doesn't exist or isn't visible to you (`Waybill not found`, `Package not found`).

409.description: A later event already exists on the package (or on any package of the waybill); resend with `ignore_conflicts: true` to record it anyway.

422.description: The waybill has no packages to record the event on (`No packages found for this waybill`).

500.description: The event could not be created.

post.description:
Prices a shipment and saves the quotation; every call saves a new one. Coordinates are required: resolve free text through `POST /api/address/resolve` first. The cheapest option wins; when no single vehicle fits, a multi-vehicle composition may be offered instead (`vehicle` null, `vehicles` set).

Signature only; a user session is not accepted. `X-Sender-Account-Id` is optional here: without it the quote has no owner, and the first sender of your organization to open it with Get a quote becomes its owner. A sender named here must belong to your organization (403 `forbidden` otherwise).

Errors answer `{ error, detail, request_id }` (`QuoteCreateError`), except the 401 and 403, which answer `{ error }`.

post.description:
Creates the order (waybill and delivery) from the quote, marks the quote `accepted`, then starts the payment. Creating the order is idempotent: calling Pay again reuses it, so a failed payment can be retried with another method. The order stays when the payment step fails.

`qr` and `app` pay through FlashPay, which settles in THB: the gateway amount is converted, the payment itself stays in the quote's currency. `bank_transfer` returns a receiving account and a reference code. `wallet` pays from the sender's prepaid balance and dispatches the order at once.

An ownerless quote must be opened with Get a quote first; Pay does not claim it.

Signature only; a user session is not accepted. The sender account is named in `X-Sender-Account-Id`, which is outside the signature: it must belong to the organization of the API key. Missing header: 401 `unauthenticated`. Malformed, unknown or another organization's account: 403 `forbidden` (the same answer for all three).

An order already created from the quote stays payable after `expires_at`: its price was fixed when it was created. `no_bank_account_available`: no receiving account can take this payment. `insufficient_balance`: the wallet does not cover it.

get.description:
Live tracking of an order created by Pay. `{id}` is the order (delivery) ID — `deliveryId` from Pay, or `delivery.id` from Get a quote — not the quotation ID.

Until the order can be tracked, the answer is still HTTP 200 but only `{ state }` (`OrderTrackingPending`): check for `state` before reading it as tracking. Results are cached for 5 seconds, so polling faster gains nothing.

Signature only; a user session is not accepted. The sender account is named in `X-Sender-Account-Id`, which is outside the signature: it must belong to the organization of the API key.
